```{r}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)

#load data
train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")
data_test <- read_csv("data-test.csv")

#transform data
#making new variables for our summary stats

#mean = R_moment_1, C_moment_2 is variance, everything else is as commented
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1, m2 = R_moment_2, m3 = R_moment_3, m4 = R_moment_4,

    # central moments
    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,                               # variance
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    # standardized versions
    sd_R     = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,                       # raw kurtosis
    ex_kurt  = kurtosis - 3                               # excess kurtosis
  )


```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Sensitivity of log_m1.5 to row 82
# Assumes `train`, `log_m1.5`, and loo_rmse() already exist.
# ============================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)

# ---- 0. Find the row ------------------------------------------
# The plot labels are ROW NAMES, which match row numbers only if `train`
# was never filtered or reordered. Check:
idx <- which(rownames(train) == "82")
idx
train[idx, c("St", "Re", "Fr", "kurtosis")]

# Which cell is it in, and how many rows does that cell have?
table(train$Re, train$Fr)            # find the cell of row 82 in this table
log(train$kurtosis[idx])             # observed
fitted(log_m1.5)[idx]                # predicted (observed is far below it)

# ---- 1. Refit without it --------------------------------------
train_no82 <- train[-idx, ]
log_m1.5_d <- update(log_m1.5, data = train_no82)

# ---- 2. Compare coefficients side by side ---------------------------
ci_full <- confint(log_m1.5)
ci_drop <- confint(log_m1.5_d)

comparison <- tibble(
  term       = names(coef(log_m1.5)),
  full       = coef(log_m1.5),
  dropped    = coef(log_m1.5_d)[names(coef(log_m1.5))],
  change     = dropped - full,
  se_full    = summary(log_m1.5)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"][names(coef(log_m1.5))],
  change_in_se = change / se_full,                      # change in units of its own standard error
  ci_full    = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", ci_full[, 1], ci_full[, 2]),
  ci_dropped = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", ci_drop[names(coef(log_m1.5)), 1],
                                       ci_drop[names(coef(log_m1.5)), 2])
)
print(comparison, width = Inf)
# Rule of thumb: |change_in_se| under ~0.5 is negligible; over ~1 is notable.

# ---- 3. The headline quantity: the St slope -------------------
b_full <- coef(log_m1.5)["log(St)"]
b_drop <- coef(log_m1.5_d)["log(St)"]
c(full = 2^b_full, dropped = 2^b_drop)     # factor change in kurtosis per doubling of St

# ---- 4. Cell baselines (fitted level at a typical St) ---------
typ <- median(log(train$St))
emm_full <- summary(emmeans(log_m1.5,   ~ Re * Fr, at = list(St = exp(typ))))
emm_drop <- summary(emmeans(log_m1.5_d, ~ Re * Fr, at = list(St = exp(typ))))
bind_cols(emm_full[, c("Re", "Fr", "emmean")],
          dropped = emm_drop$emmean) %>%
  mutate(diff = dropped - emmean, ratio_on_raw_scale = exp(diff))

# ---- 5. Fit quality and prediction error ----------------------
tibble(
  model = c("with row 82", "without row 82"),
  resid_sd = c(sigma(log_m1.5), sigma(log_m1.5_d)),
  loocv_rmse = c(loo_rmse(log_m1.5), loo_rmse(log_m1.5_d)),
  adj_r2 = c(summary(log_m1.5)$adj.r.squared, summary(log_m1.5_d)$adj.r.squared)
)
# The LOOCV values are on different row sets, so treat the comparison as
# "how much of the error was this one point", not as a model contest.

# ---- 6. Built-in influence measures (no refitting) ------------
dfb <- dfbetas(log_m1.5)[idx, ]            # standardised change in each coefficient
round(dfb, 2)                              # |value| > 2/sqrt(n) (~0.21) is notable
cooks.distance(log_m1.5)[idx]              # > 4/n (~0.045) worth checking
hatvalues(log_m1.5)[idx]                   # leverage
rstudent(log_m1.5)[idx]                    # studentised residual: |value| > 3 is an outlier

# ---- 7. Does the model choice change? -------------------------
# Does m1.5 still beat m2 once row 82 is gone?
log_m2_d <- update(log_m2, data = train_no82)
c(m1.5 = loo_rmse(log_m1.5_d), m2 = loo_rmse(log_m2_d))
anova(log_m1.5_d, log_m2_d)
```

# ============================================================
# Plots for log(kurtosis) ~ log(St) + Re * Fr
# Assumes `train` and `log_m1.5` exist; Re and Fr are factors.
# ============================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))

# ---- 1. Interaction plot: predicted kurtosis in each Re x Fr cell ----
# Non-parallel lines = interaction. Intervals are 95% CIs, back-transformed.
st_ref <- median(train$St)                       # evaluate cells at a typical St
emm    <- emmeans(log_m1.5, ~ Re * Fr, at = list(St = st_ref))
emm_df <- as.data.frame(summary(emm, type = "response")) %>% drop_na(response)
# (the empty Re = 398 / Fr = 0.3 cell is non-estimable and is dropped here)

p1 <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(Re, response, colour = Fr, group = Fr)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.25)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(0.25)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.12,
                position = position_dodge(0.25)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(x = "Re", y = "Predicted kurtosis (log scale)", colour = "Fr",
       title = "Kurtosis by Re and Fr",
       subtitle = paste0("Fitted at St = ", signif(st_ref, 3), ", 95% CI"))
p1
ggsave("figures/1_interaction_plot.png", p1, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

# ---- 2. Data with fitted lines and bands, by cell ---------------------
# Shows the common St slope and the cell baselines together.
cells <- train %>% group_by(Re, Fr) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(St), hi = max(St), .groups = "drop")

grid <- cells %>%
  mutate(St = map2(lo, hi, ~ exp(seq(log(.x), log(.y), length.out = 50)))) %>%
  unnest(St) %>% select(Re, Fr, St)

pr <- suppressWarnings(predict(log_m1.5, grid, interval = "confidence"))
grid <- bind_cols(grid, as_tibble(pr)) %>% mutate(across(c(fit, lwr, upr), exp))

p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = grid, aes(St, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = Re), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(St, fit, colour = Re), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = train, aes(St, kurtosis, colour = Re), alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Fr, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) + scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(x = "St (log scale)", y = "Kurtosis (log scale)",
       title = "Observed kurtosis and fitted model",
       subtitle = "Lines are parallel by design: one common St slope")
p2
ggsave("figures/2_data_and_fit.png", p2, width = 10, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)

# ---- 3. Forest plot: kurtosis ratios between Fr levels, within each Re ---
# "At Re = 90, kurtosis at Fr = Inf is 1/244 of that at Fr = 0.052", etc.
rat <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(emm, by = "Re"), type = "response", infer = TRUE)) %>%
  drop_na(ratio)

p3 <- ggplot(rat, aes(ratio, contrast)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Re, ncol = 1, labeller = label_both, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Kurtosis ratio (log scale; 1 = no difference)", y = NULL,
       title = "Effect of Fr on kurtosis, within each Re",
       subtitle = "Intervals are Tukey-adjusted 95% CIs")
p3
ggsave("figures/3_fr_ratios.png", p3, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# ---- 4. The St effect: partial-residual plot ---------------------------
# Slope of log(kurtosis) on log(St) after removing the Re x Fr structure.
png("figures/4_St_effect.png", width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 300)
termplot(log_m1.5, terms = "log(St)", partial.resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
         pch = 16, col.res = "grey40", rug = TRUE,
         xlab = "log(St)", ylab = "Partial effect on log(kurtosis)",
         main = "Effect of St (other terms held fixed)")
dev.off()
# Redraw on screen:
termplot(log_m1.5, terms = "log(St)", partial.resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
         pch = 16, col.res = "grey40", rug = TRUE,
         xlab = "log(St)", ylab = "Partial effect on log(kurtosis)")

# ---- 5. Leave-one-out predictions vs observed ---------------------------
h <- hatvalues(log_m1.5); e <- resid(log_m1.5)
loo <- tibble(row = rownames(train),
              obs = train$kurtosis,
              pred = exp(log(train$kurtosis) - e / (1 - h)),
              Re = train$Re, Fr = train$Fr)

p5 <- ggplot(loo, aes(obs, pred, colour = interaction(Re, Fr, sep = " / "))) +
  geom_abline(colour = "red") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = filter(loo, row == "82"), aes(label = "row 82"),
            hjust = -0.2, colour = "black", size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Observed kurtosis", y = "Leave-one-out predicted kurtosis",
       colour = "Re / Fr",
       title = "Out-of-sample predictions (leave-one-out)",
       subtitle = "Points near the red line are well predicted")
p5
ggsave("figures/5_loo_predictions.png", p5, width = 7.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)

```{r}
d <- train %>%
  mutate(Re = as.numeric(as.character(Re)),
         Fr = as.numeric(as.character(Fr)),     # "Inf" stays Inf
         y  = log(kurtosis))
# ---- 3. Input transformations ----------------------------------
# Fr: Box-Cox on z = 1 + 1/Fr (z >= 1, Fr = Inf -> z = 1). lambda = 1 is the inverse.
fr_bc <- function(Fr, lambda) {
  z <- 1 + 1 / Fr
  if (abs(lambda) < 1e-8) log(z) else (z^lambda - 1) / lambda
}
mu_re <- mean(log(train$Re)); sd_re <- sd(log(train$Re))
prep <- function(df, lambda) {
  ref <- fr_bc(train$Fr, lambda)
  df %>% mutate(x1 = log(St),
                x2 = (log(Re) - mu_re) / sd_re,
                x3 = (fr_bc(Fr, lambda) - mean(ref)) / sd(ref))
}
bk <- range(log(train$St)); kn <- quantile(log(train$St), c(.25, .5, .75))
B  <- function(x) ns(x, knots = kn, Boundary.knots = bk)     # spline basis for log(St)

lm_fun <- function(f) function(tr, te) suppressWarnings(predict(lm(f, tr), te))
mm <- function(df) model.matrix(~ (B(x1) + x2 + x3)^2, df)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
lasso_fun <- function(tr, te) {
  set.seed(1)
  fit <- cv.glmnet(mm(tr), tr$y, alpha = 1, nfolds = 10)
  as.numeric(predict(fit, mm(te), s = "lambda.min"))
}
models <- list(
  mean_only    = function(tr, te) rep(mean(tr$y), nrow(te)),
  linear       = lm_fun(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3),
  interactions = lm_fun(y ~ (x1 + x2 + x3)^2),
  shared_curve = lm_fun(y ~ B(x1) + x1:x2 + x1:x3 + x2 * x3),   # one curve in log St, tilted by Re, Fr
  lasso        = lasso_fun)

 
# ---- 5. Validation that matches the goal -------------------------
Re_mid <- sort(unique(train$Re))[2]; Fr_mid <- sort(unique(train$Fr))[2]
cv_pred <- function(fit_fun, dat, folds) {
  pred <- numeric(nrow(dat))
  for (g in unique(folds)) { te <- folds == g; pred[te] <- fit_fun(dat[!te, ], dat[te, ]) }
  pred
}
evaluate <- function(fit_fun, dat, reps = 5) {
  rmse <- function(pr, m = rep(TRUE, nrow(dat))) sqrt(mean((dat$y[m] - pr[m])^2))
  rand <- mean(replicate(reps, rmse(cv_pred(fit_fun, dat,
                 sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(dat)))))))
  pr_re <- cv_pred(fit_fun, dat, dat$Re); pr_fr <- cv_pred(fit_fun, dat, dat$Fr)
  c(random_10fold = rand,
    Re_interp = rmse(pr_re, dat$Re == Re_mid), Re_extrap = rmse(pr_re, dat$Re != Re_mid),
    Fr_interp = rmse(pr_fr, dat$Fr == Fr_mid), Fr_extrap = rmse(pr_fr, dat$Fr != Fr_mid))
}
 
# Tune the Fr transformation (weakly identified: Fr has only 3 distinct values)
lams <- c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3)
lam_tab <- map_dfr(lams, ~ as_tibble_row(evaluate(models$interactions, prep(d, .x))) %>%
                     mutate(lambda = .x, .before = 1))
print(lam_tab)
lambda <- 1                                   # <- choose from lam_tab and justify it
dd <- prep(d, lambda)
 
results <- map_dfr(models, ~ as_tibble_row(evaluate(.x, dd)), .id = "model")
print(results, width = Inf)                   # RMSE on the log scale; exp(RMSE) = typical error factor
 
loo_rmse <- function(m) sqrt(mean((resid(m) / (1 - hatvalues(m)))^2))
loo_rmse(lm(y ~ (x1 + x2 + x3)^2, dd))        # leave-one-out error of the interactions model
loo_rmse(models)

loo_any <- function(fit_fun, dat) {
  pr <- cv_pred(fit_fun, dat, seq_len(nrow(dat)))
  sqrt(mean((dat$y - pr)^2))
}
map_dbl(models, ~ loo_any(.x, dd))
```
